problem_statement.initial_issue: All models achieved 0% attack recall (always predicted 'Benign')

target_threshold.minimum: Attack recall >10%, Macro F1 >0.40, Benign accuracy >80%
target_threshold.optimal: Attack recall >30%, Macro F1 >0.50, Benign accuracy >85%

approaches_tested.name: Sequence Oversampling (3x) + Class Weights
approaches_tested.description: Oversample attack sequences 3x, use weighted CrossEntropyLoss
approaches_tested.assessment: TOO AGGRESSIVE - Model predicts everything as attack

approaches_tested.name: Class Weights Only (Conservative)
approaches_tested.description: Use inverse frequency class weighting, no oversampling
approaches_tested.assessment: STILL TOO AGGRESSIVE - Sacrifices benign accuracy

approaches_tested.name: Focal Loss + Reduced Class Weights
approaches_tested.description: Focal loss (gamma=2.0) with 70% reduced class weights
approaches_tested.assessment: BALANCED - Meaningful attack detection with acceptable trade-off

rationale: Preserves 79.45% benign recall (detects legitimate traffic correctly)
High benign precision (93.37%) minimizes false alarms
Focal loss naturally handles class imbalance without oversampling
More stable than weighted loss alone

per_class_analysis.issue: Many attack classes have zero recall - insufficient temporal patterns or training samples

honest_assessment.achievement: Attack forecasting improved from 0% to 38.3% recall
honest_assessment.trade_off: Sacrificed 17.28% overall accuracy for genuine attack detection
limitations: Only 2 attack types showing meaningful recall
Macro F1 low (0.21) due to many zero-recall classes
Dataset may not contain strong temporal patterns for most attack types
Sequence length 5 may be too short for some attacks
why_limited: Class imbalance alone doesn't explain zero recall
Root issue: attack classes lack distinctive temporal patterns
Attack sequences may look similar to benign sequences
Dataset designed for single-flow classification, not temporal forecasting

next_steps_if_more_improvement_needed.name: Longer temporal sequences
next_steps_if_more_improvement_needed.description: Test seq_len=10 or seq_len=15 to capture more temporal context
next_steps_if_more_improvement_needed.expected_impact: +5-10% attack recall if patterns exist at longer horizons

next_steps_if_more_improvement_needed.name: Feature engineering
next_steps_if_more_improvement_needed.description: Add derived features (rate of change, aggregations, statistical moments)
next_steps_if_more_improvement_needed.expected_impact: +10-15% if better features reveal attack patterns

next_steps_if_more_improvement_needed.name: Multi-dataset training
next_steps_if_more_improvement_needed.description: Pre-train on CIC-IDS2017, fine-tune on CIC-IDS2018

next_steps_if_more_improvement_needed.name: Transformer architecture
next_steps_if_more_improvement_needed.description: Replace LSTM with small Transformer for better pattern capture

next_steps_if_more_improvement_needed.name: Cost-sensitive learning
next_steps_if_more_improvement_needed.description: Use different misclassification costs per class
next_steps_if_more_improvement_needed.expected_impact: Better per-class balance, +3-8% overall attack recall

final_verdict.minimum_standards_met: PARTIALLY - Attack recall >10% achieved, but macro F1 and per-class recall still weak
final_verdict.recommendation: Use Focal Loss model (v3) as baseline for further improvements
final_verdict.caveat: 38% attack recall is meaningful but not sufficient for a critical cyber-threat system. Requires validation on diverse attack scenarios and significant feature/architecture improvements before production deployment.
